result.summary:
Step 12 exists, runs cleanly from a fresh R process in about 9 seconds (peak memory about 210 MB), and its outputs are in place: 13 CSV tables and 2 figures under /home/user/WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/04_output/12_qpcr/. The script is /home/user/WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/01_pipeline/12_qpcr.R (1127 lines, longest line 150 characters, ASCII only). I ran no git command that changes state; the orchestrating session's snapshot commit 9fc2f06 already holds exactly this script, the 13 tables and the 2 PNG files (the PDFs and session_info.txt differ only by time stamp after my last rerun).

What the step does. (1) Builds the per-animal table from the nine replicate-level files (40 animals, 720 wells, 149 non-detect wells) with explicit ID, group-size and Cq checks, and compares it with the hand-built consolidated file. (2) Repeats the legacy analysis on the consolidated file in both variants (non-detects dropped; set to config$qpcr$legacy_nondetect), aov plus TukeyHSD, and compares it with the knitted legacy output (parsed, not typed) and with the audit note. (3) Fits delta Cq ~ ploidy * treatment per gene three ways: complete cases; censored regression (survival::survreg, Gaussian, an animal with no detected well is right-censored at max_cycles minus its actin Cq); and the same with one-well animals as bounds. Each fit is run with all 32 animals and without failed samples, with fold changes, 95% intervals, Benjamini-Hochberg q across genes per term, leave-one-out p ranges, and, for simple effects in complete-case fits, Student and Welch tests on the two groups alone. (4) Reference gene: actin by group, group differences, failed samples by Tukey's outer fence, and every effect under three normalizations (delta Cq, raw Cq, raw Cq with actin Cq as covariate). (5) COX1 as a raw Cq with the tests the audit note lists. (6) Ten statement rows (nine sentences of the Discussion and Conclusions, quoted word for word) with numbers and rule-derived verdicts. (7) Two figures.

Main results. The consolidated file equals the mean of the detected wells in all 288 cells (9 genes x 32 animals); 44 cells are missing, all without a detected well. The legacy analysis is reproduced: 11 of 11 ANOVA tables and 88 of 88 TukeyHSD lines of the knitted output agree at the printed precision, and the 9 quoted F and p values of the audit note agree. Of the eight targets with replicate data, three are quantifiable by the MIQE 95% rule (HSC70, HATHaP2, HSP90), four are near the detection limit (DNMT1 16%, HAT 22%, MBD2 30%, HIF1A 31% non-detect wells of 64), and MeCP2 (77%) is not analysed. No term of any of the nine analysed genes passes the correction across genes (smallest q: heat 0.27, ploidy 0.49, interaction 0.54). HSP90, primary analysis (censored regression without the failed sample D_N_N05, actin Cq 35.26, outer fence 33.38): heat vs control 2.17-fold (95% CI 1.08 to 4.34, p = 0.030); triploid vs diploid 1.95-fold (0.98 to 3.91, p = 0.058); in control animals 2.10-fold (0.77 to 5.68), p = 0.139 in the two-way model and 0.031 (Welch) or 0.033 (Student) on the two control groups alone. The legacy ploidy p = 0.035 exists only when the failed sample's non-detect is set to Cq 45. Actin differs between ploidies by -1.68 cycles (p = 0.078) and, without the failed sample, between heat and control by 1.14 cycles (p = 0.12); within groups the target Cq follows the actin Cq with a slope below 1 for most genes (HSC70 0.68, 95% CI 0.56 to 0.80). The HSP90 heat effect is 2.17-fold as delta Cq, 1.90-fold (p = 0.077) with actin as covariate and 0.99-fold (p = 0.98) in raw Cq, while the ploidy effect keeps its direction (1.95, 2.21, 4.11-fold). COX1: group means within 0.29 cycles, heat minus control -0.19 cycles in diploids (p = 0.37) and +0.29 in triploids (p = 0.083), interaction p = 0.070, correlation with actin Cq 0.002, no nuclear reference. Verdicts: the six rows on mitochondrial abundance are not supported; the four rows on HSP90 are partly supported, with conditions.

What I could not do: nothing in the repository gives primer efficiencies, the COX1 template, or replicate-level data for SOD, ATP synthetase and COX1, so those limits stay. I did not edit README files, issues.md or run_config.R; proposed text is in the fields below.
key_results: Consolidated file check (qpcr_consolidated_check.csv): 9 genes x 32 animals = 288 cells, 0 differ from the mean of the detected wells (largest absolute difference 0 at six decimals); 44 missing cells (MeCP2 18, DNMT1 5, MBD2 6, HIF1A 6, HAT 4, HATHaP2 1, HSP90 1, SOD 1, ATP synthetase 2). SOD, ATP synthetase and COX1 cannot be checked: no replicate-level file.

Legacy analysis reproduced (qpcr_anova_legacy.csv, qpcr_tukey_legacy.csv): 11 of 11 genes agree with the knitted legacy output at the printed precision (sum of squares, F and p of all three terms); 88 of 88 printed TukeyHSD lines agree; 9 of 9 F and p values quoted in the audit note agree. Example, HSP90 with non-detects at 45: ploidy F(1,28) = 4.899, p = 0.0352; treatment F = 6.386, p = 0.0174; interaction p = 0.683. Non-detects dropped: ploidy F(1,27) = 3.614, p = 0.068; treatment F = 5.223, p = 0.030; interaction p = 0.836.

Detection (qpcr_nondetects.csv): non-detect wells of 80 are MeCP2 60, HIF1A 28, MBD2 23, HAT 17, DNMT1 15, HSP90 3, HATHaP2 2, Actin 1, HSC70 0. Classes for the 32 animals: quantifiable HSC70, HATHaP2, HSP90, SOD; near the detection limit DNMT1, MBD2, HIF1A, HAT, ATP synthetase; not analysed MeCP2 (detected in 23% of wells; lowest group 19%). Without the failed sample ATP synthetase becomes quantifiable.
No effect survives correction across the nine analysed genes (qpcr_models.csv, primary analysis): smallest q is 0.27 for heat (HSP90), 0.49 for ploidy (HSP90), 0.54 for the interaction (HAT).

HSP90 (primary analysis): heat vs control 2.17-fold (95% CI 1.08 to 4.34), p = 0.030, q = 0.27; within diploids 2.33-fold (0.86 to 6.31), p = 0.094; within triploids 2.02-fold (0.77 to 5.30), p = 0.146; interaction p = 0.836. Triploid vs diploid 1.95-fold (0.98 to 3.91), p = 0.058, q = 0.49; in control animals 2.10-fold (0.77 to 5.68), p = 0.139 in the model, Welch p = 0.031 and Student p = 0.033 on the two control groups alone (q = 0.28 and 0.30), legacy Tukey p = 0.44 (dropped) and 0.27 (set to 45).
Leave-one-out (qpcr_models.csv): the HSP90 heat p ranges from 0.015 to 0.055 and the ploidy p from 0.007 (without D_D_N11) to 0.106 (without T_D_N11) when one animal is left out.

Failed sample: D_N_N05 has actin Cq 35.26, above the outer fence of 33.38 (quartiles 24.18 and 26.48); 6 of its 8 targets with replicate data have no detected well. With 45 substituted it is the highest 'expression' of DNMT1 and HAT and the lowest of HSP90, which moves the HSP90 ploidy p from 0.058 to 0.035. Excluding it changes HSC70 most (ploidy p 0.351 to 0.765, treatment p 0.988 to 0.291) because its HSC70 was detected at a delta Cq of 1.9.

Reference gene (qpcr_reference_gene.csv, qpcr_normalization_check.csv): actin Cq 21.9 to 35.3; triploid minus diploid -1.68 cycles (95% CI -3.57 to 0.20, p = 0.078; -1.07 cycles, p = 0.144 without the failed sample); heat minus control 1.14 cycles without the failed sample (-0.32 to 2.60, p = 0.122). Within-group slope of target Cq on actin Cq (1 if actin tracks the template): HSC70 0.68 (0.56 to 0.80), HATHaP2 0.59, SOD 0.54, DNMT1 0.69, HAT 0.69, MBD2 0.44, HIF1A 0.45, HSP90 0.83 (0.57 to 1.10), ATP synthetase 0.88.

Normalization moves the HSP90 heat result: 2.17-fold (p = 0.030) as delta Cq, 1.90-fold (p = 0.077) with actin Cq as covariate, 0.99-fold (p = 0.978) in raw Cq. The HSP90 ploidy effect keeps its direction: 1.95-fold (p = 0.058), 2.21-fold (p = 0.031), 4.11-fold (p = 0.012). Under delta Cq seven of nine genes read as higher in heat animals.

Treatment of non-detects decides MBD2: heat effect p = 0.009 with non-detects dropped, 0.671 with 45 substituted, 0.090 in the censored regression (qpcr_sensitivity.csv). Reading one-well animals as bounds changes the near-limit genes (MBD2 ploidy 0.91-fold to 1.53-fold; HIF1A interaction 0.52-fold to 1.06-fold) and leaves HSP90 nearly unchanged (ploidy 2.02-fold, p = 0.054; heat 2.10-fold, p = 0.043).

COX1 (qpcr_cox1.csv): raw Cq means 21.54 (SD 0.25), 21.36 (0.50), 21.36 (0.27), 21.64 (0.34) for diploid control, diploid heat, triploid control, triploid heat; range 20.845 to 22.440; heat minus control -0.185 cycles in diploids (Student p = 0.365, Welch 0.371) and +0.288 cycles in triploids (Student p = 0.083, Welch 0.084); interaction F(1,28) = 3.56, p = 0.070; smallest Tukey p = 0.382; correlation with actin Cq 0.002, against 0.53 to 0.93 (median 0.73) for the nine analysed targets. No nuclear reference, so relative mitochondrial abundance is not estimable.

Statement verdicts (qpcr_manuscript_statements.csv, 10 rows from 9 sentences in Discussion 4.2, 4.5, 4.7 and Conclusions 4.9): Q01 to Q04, Q08 and Q10 (mitochondrial abundance) not supported; Q05, Q07 and Q09 (HSP90 higher in triploid controls) partly supported: p < 0.05 only in tests of the two control groups alone, and not after correction across 9 genes; Q06 (heat raises HSP90 in both ploidies) partly supported: only when the two ploidies are averaged, not after correction across 9 genes, only if actin is a valid reference for the heat comparison, and not in every fit that leaves one animal out.
The audit note's assessment in section 3.3 (induction by heat as the better-supported HSP90 effect) needs correcting: the heat effect is the one that depends on normalization to actin.
validation: Determinism: two consecutive runs from fresh R processes, plus a third run sourced inside an R session, gave byte-identical md5 sums for all 13 CSV tables and both PNG figures. Exit status 0, no warning or error in the logs.
Runs through the pipeline runner: Rscript run_pipeline.R --steps 12 finished in 0.1 min.
No hidden warnings: a sandbox copy run with options(warn = 2) completes.

Audit note, sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 4: 92 quoted qPCR values looked up in the output CSVs only (scratch script check_audit_numbers.R): 92 of 92 agree at the quoted precision. Several sit exactly on a rounding boundary (for example 8.39375 against 8.394) and agree within half a unit of the last digit.

Section 3.3, HSP90 tests, quoted -> regenerated. Non-detects at 45: ploidy F(1,28) 4.90 -> 4.89925, p 0.035 -> 0.0351874, triploid over diploid 2.09 -> 2.089; treatment F 6.39 -> 6.38632, p 0.017 -> 0.0174287, heat over control 2.32 -> 2.3189; interaction p 0.68 -> 0.682558; Tukey triploid control vs diploid control 0.27 -> 0.268974. Complete case: ploidy F(1,27) 3.61 -> 3.61412, p 0.068 -> 0.0680146; treatment F 5.22 -> 5.22296, p 0.030 -> 0.0303659; interaction p 0.84 -> 0.835958; Tukey 0.44 -> 0.437997. Control-only t test: 0.033 -> 0.0331253 (qpcr_models.csv, p_two_groups_student) and 0.016 -> 0.016 (numbers column of qpcr_manuscript_statements.csv). Actin Cq of D_C_N_05: 35.26 -> 35.255.

Other audit values reproduced: non-detect wells per 80 for all nine genes; 44 missing cells, 18 for MeCP2; COX1 range 20.845 to 22.440; r of COX1 with actin 0.002; actin range 21.9 to 35.3; actin ploidy p 0.078 -> 0.0779408; five targets with a well-level median Cq of 37 to 38; MeCP2 75% non-detect wells; HSP90 2^-delta Cq top three 0.1015, 0.0998, 0.0602 (D_D_N11, T_D_N11, T_D_N12).

Knitted legacy output: the script itself parses 08_archive/ELISA/dct_analysis_NA-to-45_COX1convert.md and reports 11 of 11 ANOVA tables and 88 of 88 TukeyHSD lines in agreement; a separate scratch parser (check_tukey_vs_knitted.R) gave the same 88 of 88.

Independent recomputation of qpcr_models.csv from the raw files by another route (formula interface with sum-to-zero coding, emmeans for simple effects; scratch check_models_independent.R): 252 rows for complete cases and censored regression; largest difference 4.3e-10 in estimates, 5.0e-11 in p and in q, 5.0e-10 in confidence limits. The bounds analysis (check_bounds_independent.R): 42 rows, largest difference 4.1e-10 in estimates and 4.9e-11 in p; censored counts equal.

Censored regression against a direct maximisation of the right-censored Gaussian likelihood with optim (check_censored_ml.R), all nine analysed genes: group means within 3.7e-7 cycles, p of the treatment term within 3.0e-7.

Built-in assertion: for a gene with no censored animal the censored regression must equal the linear model (estimates, standard errors, p within 1e-6) or the script stops. It holds for HSC70 in both animal sets and for HATHaP2, HSP90 and SOD without the failed sample.

Small-sample calibration (scratch simulation sim_calibration.R, 3000 runs per gene under the null with the real censoring bounds of the 31 animals): the uncorrected maximum-likelihood z test rejects 7.1% to 8.8% at a nominal 5%; the corrected t test used in the step rejects 4.5% to 6.0% (Monte Carlo standard error 0.4 points), including genes with 14% to 27% censored animals.

Treatment of non-detects (scratch simulation sim1.R of well-level data, 1500 runs per scenario): substituting 45 biased the ploidy contrast by up to -0.19 cycles and the interaction by up to -0.65 cycles and halved power (0.29 against 0.61); complete cases biased the interaction by -0.16 to -0.44 cycles; the censored regression of the step by -0.04 to -0.25; treating one-well animals as bounds by -0.05 to 0.06.

Quoted statements: all 10 rows found word for word in the local manuscript text (lines 68, 78, 79, 80, 105, 112); section and paragraph positions checked against the headings (scratch check_quotes.R).

Sandbox copies of the repository, inputs or settings that must stop the step, each with a clear message: malformed replicate ID; malformed consolidated ID; detected Cq above max_cycles; unreadable Cq text; a missing well; an animal missing from every file; wrong header; treatment code contradicting the animal number; text in a consolidated gene column; missing knitted legacy file; altered legacy ANOVA table; unknown reference gene; unknown mito gene; max_cycles below a detected Cq.

Sandbox variations that must run, and do: untouched copy (13 tables identical to the repository run); include_acute_heat_shock = TRUE (40 animals); no failed sample (fence multiplier 100; both animal sets then give identical p); one consolidated value changed (reported as 1 differing cell, D_C_N_01, and HSP90 flagged as not agreeing with the legacy output); min_detected 0.1 (MeCP2 fitted by two analyses, the bounds analysis left empty because a group has fewer than two exact animals); an extra replicate file for a gene absent from the consolidated file; a replicate-level file for COX1; alpha 0.10 (verdicts change as the rules say).

Figures: both PNGs inspected with the Read tool after the final run (panels ordered by detection class, every animal one mark, non-detects as open triangles at their upper limit, failed sample ringed, group means as bars, legends for ploidy and detection). The fence line no longer stretches the axis when it lies far above the data.

Colours: config$colours$ploidy (royalblue1, orangered1) passes the dataviz palette validator on all checks (worst colour-vision pair 32.0, normal vision 40.0). The treatment pair fails the chroma check (grey35 is grey by design), so treatment is on the x axis and not encoded by colour.

Citations checked online: McCall et al. 2014 (Bioinformatics 30:2310, doi and abstract); Bustin et al. 2009 MIQE (text of sections 7.4.3 and 8.1 read from a copy of the paper); Tobin 1958; Livak and Schmittgen 2001; Ruxton 2006; Quiros et al. 2017. Not checked online, cited from memory: Benjamini and Hochberg 1995, Welch 1947, Brown and Forsythe 1974, Vandesompele et al. 2002, Tukey 1977.
Style: no non-ASCII character in the script or the tables; no setwd, rstudioapi, install.packages or absolute path; the legacy word appears only as the legacy factor name 'Desiccation'.
caveats: Every delta Cq result is conditional on actin, the only reference gene, and the data argue against it as a stable reference (group differences of 1.1 to 1.7 cycles, within-group slopes below 1). The step reports this; it cannot repair it.

The primary analysis (censored regression without failed samples), the failed-sample rule (outer fence), the detection thresholds (95% and 50%) and the verdict rules (alpha 0.05, q 0.05, leave-one-out, normalization) are choices made in this step. All variants are in the tables, and the choices are settings at the top of the script, but the authors may choose differently.

An animal with one detected well of two is taken at that well in the main censored fit and as a bound in the second censored fit. The data cannot say which is right. For HAT, HIF1A and MBD2 (6 to 8 such animals each) the two fits differ, so these genes carry no firm estimate.

Margins are thin in two places: HSP90 is quantifiable with 61 of 64 wells detected (95.3%) in the all-animal set, and HAT sits exactly on the 50% threshold in diploid controls (8 of 16 wells). One more non-detect would change either class.

Two diploid heat animals with late actin (D_D_N11 at 30.02 and D_D_N16 at 31.47) lie above the inner fence but below the outer fence and stay in. D_D_N11 has unshifted targets and drives results: without it the HSP90 ploidy p is 0.007 and the heat p 0.052.

The small-sample correction of the censored regression is exact only when nothing is censored; with censoring it rests on my scratch simulation (4.5% to 6.0% rejection at 5%), which is not part of the repository.

Residuals of the complete-case fits depart from normality for DNMT1 (Shapiro p = 0.031), HATHaP2 (0.006), HIF1A (0.025), MBD2 (0.008) and SOD (0.010); the values are in qpcr_models.csv. No rank-based or robust alternative was added.
Simple effects are not adjusted for the four simple effects of a gene, and fold changes assume doubling per cycle; no primer efficiencies are in the repository.
SOD and ATP synthetase come from the consolidated file only: their detection class counts animals instead of wells, and one-well animals cannot be told from two-well animals.
The step reads one file from 08_archive (the knitted legacy output) and stops if it is absent. Other pipeline steps do not read the archive.

The quoted sentences are typed into the script from the Google Doc text of 2026-11-18. The step cannot detect later edits of the manuscript; locations are section, paragraph and sentence of that version.

Statement Q08 also names 5-mC changes, which belong to step 03 and are not evaluated here. The draft's phrase 'companion experiments' is not evaluated; by their IDs the qPCR animals are the same 32 animals as in the ELISA (an inference from the IDs).

The script is 1127 lines, four times the size of other steps, because I was told to keep step-specific functions inside it. The fitting and legacy-parsing functions could move to 02_R_functions later.
With include_acute_heat_shock = TRUE the acute animals are pooled into their treatment group; that path runs and was looked at once, but its results were not examined in detail.
PDF figures and session_info.txt carry a time stamp and show as modified in git after any rerun; CSV and PNG files do not.
result.settings_needed:
Defined in the marked block at the top of 01_pipeline/12_qpcr.R as additions to config$qpcr (the block is merged as opt <- c(config$qpcr, list(...)), so a value of the same name placed in run_config.R takes precedence without editing the script; the block can then be deleted):

  include_acute_heat_shock = FALSE   # TRUE puts the 8 animals given the acute heat shock into the models
  mito_gene        = "COX1"          # measured without a reference gene; never normalized
  lod_detected     = 0.95            # a gene is "quantifiable" when at least this share of its wells is detected (MIQE section 7.4.3)
  min_detected     = 0.5             # a gene is not analysed when a group has a smaller share of detected wells
  failed_fence_iqr = 3               # reference Cq above Q3 + this many interquartile ranges marks a failed sample
  conf_level       = 0.95            # confidence level of the intervals
  alpha            = 0.05            # unadjusted p value used in the verdicts
  fdr              = 0.05            # Benjamini-Hochberg q value used in the verdicts
  cq_tolerance     = 0.0005          # two Cq values agree when they differ by no more than half of the third decimal

Not settings, kept in the script as facts about the files or the draft: design <- list(wells_per_animal = 2, animals_per_group = 8, acute_per_group = 2, nondetect_text = "N/A"); hsp <- "HSP90" (the expression gene the draft names); the primary analysis (censored regression, failed samples excluded) is fixed in code and could become a setting if the authors want another default.

result.issues_text:
### I-29 (S2) qPCR and "mitochondrial abundance" claims

Proposed status in the summary table: `needs decision; pipeline done (step 12)`.

**Update 2026-11-19 (step 12, `01_pipeline/12_qpcr.R`; tables in `04_output/12_qpcr/tables/`).** Every number below is regenerated by the step.
- *Inputs.* The hand-built consolidated file equals the mean of the detected wells of the replicate-level files in all 288 cells (9 genes x 32 animals). Its 44 missing cells are animals with no detected well (`qpcr_consolidated_check.csv`). SOD, ATP synthetase and COX1 exist only in the consolidated file.
- *Legacy analysis reproduced.* 11 of 11 ANOVA tables and 88 of 88 TukeyHSD lines of `08_archive/ELISA/dct_analysis_NA-to-45_COX1convert.md` agree at the printed precision; the nine F and p values quoted in the audit note agree (`qpcr_anova_legacy.csv`, `qpcr_tukey_legacy.csv`).
- *Mitochondrial abundance.* Group means of the raw COX1 Cq are 21.54, 21.36, 21.36 and 21.64 (diploid control, diploid heat, triploid control, triploid heat). Heat minus control is -0.19 cycles in diploids (p = 0.37) and +0.29 cycles in triploids (p = 0.083); interaction p = 0.070; smallest Tukey p = 0.38. The COX1 Cq does not follow the actin Cq (r = 0.002; the nine analysed targets: r = 0.53 to 0.93), which points to a separate template. No nuclear reference was measured on it, so no relative abundance can be formed (`qpcr_cox1.csv`). Six statement rows: not supported.
- *HSP90.* This replaces the earlier sentence that the clearer effect is induction by heat. Relative to actin, heat vs control is 2.17-fold (95% CI 1.08 to 4.34; p = 0.030; q = 0.27 across nine genes); within diploids p = 0.094, within triploids p = 0.146; interaction p = 0.84. Triploid vs diploid is 1.95-fold (0.98 to 3.91; p = 0.058; q = 0.49); in control animals 2.10-fold (0.77 to 5.68), p = 0.139 in the two-way model, p = 0.031 (Welch) and 0.033 (Student) in a test of the two control groups alone, Tukey p = 0.44. The legacy ploidy p = 0.035 arises only when the non-detect of the failed sample D_N_N05 is set to Cq 45. With one animal left out the heat p ranges from 0.015 to 0.055 and the ploidy p from 0.007 to 0.106. The heat effect depends on the normalization (new issue below); the ploidy difference keeps its direction under each normalization (`qpcr_models.csv`, `qpcr_normalization_check.csv`). Four statement rows: partly supported, with the conditions listed in `qpcr_manuscript_statements.csv`.
- *Several genes.* The legacy analysis normalized ten targets to actin and the draft names one. Across the nine genes that can be analysed no term has q < 0.05 (smallest q: heat 0.27, ploidy 0.49, interaction 0.54).
- *Design.* By their IDs the qPCR animals are the 32 animals of the ELISA (control 01 to 08 and heat 11 to 18 of each ploidy), so the qPCR, unlike the WGBS comparison (I-01), compares control and heat animals of one experiment. The draft calls them "companion experiments"; to be confirmed by the authors.
- The assessment in `07_documentation/audit/elisa_qpcr_audit.md`, section 3.3, needs the same correction.

**Options (extended).** (a) Remove the qPCR statements. (b) Keep HSP90 as an exploratory observation: describe the assay in Methods, report fold changes with intervals from `qpcr_models.csv`, and state that one unvalidated reference gene was used and that no effect survives correction across the genes measured. (c) For any statement about mitochondria, measure COX1 against a single-copy nuclear gene on the same DNA. Triploid nuclei hold 1.5 times the nuclear DNA, so a ratio to a nuclear gene needs that factor before ploidies are compared.

### I-xx (S2) Actin, the only reference gene, does not behave as a stable reference

**Evidence (step 12; `qpcr_reference_gene.csv`, `qpcr_normalization_check.csv`).** Actin Cq spans 21.9 to 35.3 across the 32 animals. It differs between ploidies by -1.68 cycles (95% CI -3.57 to 0.20; p = 0.078; -1.07 cycles, p = 0.14 without the failed sample) and, without the failed sample, between heat and control by 1.14 cycles (-0.32 to 2.60; p = 0.12). Within groups a target Cq rises by less than one cycle per cycle of actin: HSC70 0.68 (0.56 to 0.80), HATHaP2 0.59, SOD 0.54, HSP90 0.83 (0.57 to 1.10), ATP synthetase 0.88. Delta Cq therefore still depends on the amount of template, and animals with a late actin Cq read as high expressers. For HSP90, heat vs control is 2.17-fold as delta Cq, 1.90-fold (p = 0.077) with the actin Cq as covariate, and 0.99-fold (p = 0.98) in raw Cq. Under delta Cq seven of nine genes read as higher in heat animals.

**Why it matters.** Normalization to one reference gene needs evidence that the gene is stable under the conditions compared (Bustin et al. 2009, Clinical Chemistry 55:611, section 8.1). Every relative expression in the legacy analysis rests on actin.

**Needs.** Information from the authors (was a second reference gene run; RNA input and quality per sample) and a decision.

### I-xx (S2) Most qPCR targets were measured at or below their limit of detection

**Evidence (`qpcr_nondetects.csv`).** Non-detect wells among the 64 wells of the 32 animals: HSC70 0, HATHaP2 2, HSP90 3, DNMT1 10 (16%), HAT 14 (22%), MBD2 19 (30%), HIF1A 20 (31%), MeCP2 49 (77%). At the limit of detection 95% of wells are detected (Bustin et al. 2009, section 7.4.3), so of the eight targets with replicate-level data only HSC70, HATHaP2 and HSP90 are quantifiable. MeCP2 has no group with half its wells detected and is not analysed. For HAT, HIF1A and MBD2 six to eight animals have one detected well of two, and the result depends on how that well is read (MBD2 ploidy 0.91-fold or 1.53-fold; HIF1A interaction 0.52-fold or 1.06-fold; `qpcr_models.csv`).

**Proposed resolution.** Do not report DNMT1, MBD2, MeCP2, HIF1A or HAT as quantitative results.

### I-xx (S2) Substituting Cq 45 for non-detects creates values

**Evidence (`qpcr_sensitivity.csv`, `qpcr_reference_gene.csv`).** The runs had 40 cycles (latest detected Cq 39.94), so no well can have a Cq of 45. With 45 substituted and actin subtracted, the failed sample D_N_N05 (actin Cq 35.26, above the outer fence of 33.38; 6 of its 8 targets have no detected well) becomes the highest "expression" of DNMT1 and HAT and the lowest of HSP90, which moves the HSP90 ploidy p from 0.058 to 0.035. For MBD2 the heat effect has p = 0.009 with non-detects dropped, 0.67 with 45 substituted, and 0.090 in the censored regression. Both legacy treatments are biased (McCall et al. 2014, Bioinformatics 30:2310).

**Status.** pipeline done (step 12): both legacy variants are reproduced, and a censored regression is reported beside them.
